title: CSPs & Backtracking Search
html:
A constraint satisfaction problem (CSP) describes a state as variables with domains and the goal as a set of constraints. That factored structure lets one general-purpose solver handle map colouring, Sudoku, scheduling and timetabling — and prune huge parts of the search space.

CSP — a triple (X, D, C): variables X₁…Xₙ, a domain Dᵢ of allowed values for each, and constraints C that restrict which combinations of values are allowed. A solution is a complete and consistent assignment — every variable has a value and no constraint is violated.

Example: colouring the map of Australia

PartMap colouring
VariablesWA, NT, SA, Q, NSW, V, T (the seven states and territories)
Domains{red, green, blue} for each
ConstraintsNeighbouring regions differ: WA ≠ NT, WA ≠ SA, NT ≠ SA, NT ≠ Q, SA ≠ Q, SA ≠ NSW, SA ≠ V, Q ≠ NSW, NSW ≠ V

Binary constraints form a constraint graph: nodes are variables, edges connect variables that share a constraint. Tasmania (T) has no edges — an independent sub-problem.

Kinds of constraints and problems

KindExample
Unary (one variable)SA ≠ green
Binary (two variables)WA ≠ NT
Global / higher-orderAlldiff(F, T, U, W, R, O) in cryptarithmetic; each Sudoku row/column/box
Preference (soft)“Prof. X prefers mornings” → a constraint optimisation problem
Sudoku: 81 variables, domain 1–9, 27 Alldiff constraintsN-queensexam timetablingjob-shop schedulingSEND + MORE = MONEYcircuit layoutregister allocation (graph colouring)

Backtracking search

Backtracking is depth-first search that assigns one variable per level, checks constraints immediately and undoes the last choice when no value fits. Because assignment order doesn't matter (commutativity), it explores dⁿ leaves instead of the n!·dⁿ a naive search would.

Counting every solution: 8-queens

Key point

Plain backtracking already beats generate-and-test (8⁸ ≈ 16.8 million full boards) by checking constraints on partial assignments. The next topic makes it smarter: choose variables and values wisely, and propagate constraints ahead.

What is a CSP? Give an example.

A problem defined by variables, domains and constraints, solved by finding an assignment that satisfies all constraints. Examples: map colouring, Sudoku, N-queens, timetabling.

Why is backtracking better than plain DFS over assignments?

It fixes one variable per tree level (assignments commute) and checks constraints as soon as a variable is assigned, abandoning a partial assignment the moment it violates a constraint instead of completing it first.
